Village News

Project Purple raised $400, and a warm welcome to Ross

As we head into November, it's hard to believe how quickly the year has flown by! With the festive season just around the corner, there's plenty to look forward to, and we're excited for all the celebrations and activities coming up across the Village.

A big thank you to everyone who supported Project Purple! Together, we raised a fantastic $400, which is a wonderful effort for such a meaningful cause. It was lovely to see our community come together, we truly appreciate everyone's generosity, contributions, & support. The winners of the Project Purple raffles are — Mandy South – Tote bag, Lorriane Bullock – Bucket bag & Jenny Mills – $50. Congratulations to all!

It's certainly been a busy time around the Village, with plenty of activities taking place alongside our ongoing refurbishment works. Thank you all for your patience and understanding as we work through these improvements.

I'm pleased to share that the MRC refurbishment remains on track, and our recent resident presentation went well. It was a great opportunity to share the plans, provide an update on our progress and give everyone a glimpse of what's to come. We're looking forward to seeing the finished space and all the opportunities it will bring for our community.

I'd also like to extend a warm welcome to Ross, our new Maintenance Supervisor. Ross has joined the team and is settling into his role, so please make him feel welcome when you see him around the Village. You'll also notice a contract gardener, working throughout the grounds and helping Gary to keep our Village looking its best.

As we approach the festive season, I hope everyone enjoys the activities, celebrations, and opportunities to come together over the coming weeks. It's a lovely time of year, and I'm looking forward to sharing the festivities with you all.

Thank you again for your continued patience, kindness, and support.

Warm regards, Candice.

Emergency Evacuation Exercise

Monday 2 November 2026, from 1:30pm in the Manor.

This exercise forms part of our regular emergency preparedness training and provides our team with an opportunity to practise their response to an emergency, including evacuation procedures and resident safety.

Residents are warmly invited to participate in the exercise. While participation is voluntary, we encourage residents who are interested to join us. It is a valuable opportunity to become more familiar with our emergency procedures and understand what to expect should an actual emergency occur.

Village Pest Control Program

EBS Pest Management will be onsite to commence treatment throughout the village from Monday 9th November. Treatment dates are as per the 23rd October notice distributed.

Please advise if you will be absent on the day scheduled for treatment but give permission for staff to allow EBS entry — please let reception know by calling 3862 9020.

The cost of the Pest Control and Visual Termite inspection is included in your service fees, so no payment is required. If you request further treatments ie termite barriers etc this would be at your cost.

Please note this schedule is subject to change, however EBS will endeavour to keep to the above.

Maintenance Related

Settings on your air conditioner remote can be changed depending on the weather and temperature.

  • Cool — removes heat from the room
  • Dry — reduces humidity levels in the room
  • Heat — blows warm air into the room

During the evenings if you notice any lights not working — please advise the office.

Dogs (excluding assistance dogs)

Please remember no pets are permitted in communal areas of the Village unless permission granted.

If you have a loved one visiting and there is a dog — the dog must be carried whilst outside of your unit if indoors. The only exception is for assistance dogs.

Testing Your Tunstall

Test your pendant and base unit monthly. If you are unsure on how to carry out these tests — please speak to the office.

Reminder: have an overnight bag packed in case of an emergency. Keep a list of your current medications with it.

Sales News

November is here, and the last quarter until Christmas!

We didn't have an Open House in October as we don't have very many units to sell. I've got a couple that is in the vacate process and one ILU that is going through works.

Don't forget our referral program where the company will pay you if you refer someone to join us in the Village. We have already had some referrals, and those residents can enjoy their $1,000 which is credited to their account. Aveo also give a $1,000 to the incoming resident as well as $1,000 to the Community to spend on whatever you want. That's a nice incentive!!! So, who do you know that would benefit our Village.

We have had 1 deposit in October for an ILU.

We are now looking down the barrel to Christmas and all the fun activities we do.

Warm regards, Debbie and Chatalia

Social

Social Club News

The Month That Was

Oh, what a night! The Manor was rocking on 3 October at the Dance Party featuring musical entertainment by Fortunato Isgro. Photos taken at this event have been posted to the Residents' Information Hub (bdrv.au/event-gallery.html) where any resident is welcome to post photos taken at Aveo Bridgeman Downs events and activities. About 25 residents backed up the next night to watch the NRL Grand Final on the big screen in The Manor.

On 15 October, Anne Macdonald from Uniforms 4 Kids provided insight into this charity and the work undertaken by volunteers to transform donated law enforcement and emergency services uniforms into clothes for needy children. The morning tea which followed allowed further discussion and questions and as a consequence there has been considerable interest from residents in becoming involved in some way. Watch for an update early in 2027 on how this can happen! A donation of $500 has been made to Uniforms 4 Kids as a result of this event.

Six residents took advantage of a free Chess coaching session on 16 October provided by a professional chess coach, Ross Lam. If anyone is interested in playing chess, join Tony Keogh in The Manor on Monday 9 November at 4pm. Hopefully this will be the start of regular chess games.

John Finglas (unit 255) was the winner of the October raffle ($50 Dan Murphy's voucher, and a plant and planter) while Joy Gallagher (unit 262) won the second prize of 2 bottles of wine.

International Men's Day

19 November 2026. Celebrate the positive value and contributions that men bring to their families and communities.

World Kindness Day

World Kindness Day is celebrated all over the globe on November 13. The purpose of World Kindness Day is to encourage people to be kind to each other and thus spread kindness in their communities.

Remembrance Day

Tuesday, 11 November. Honour • Remember • Together. We honour the courage, sacrifice and service of all who have served and sacrificed for our freedom. We will remember them.

National Recycling Week

9th – 15th November. Turn waste into a resource. Every can, bottle, and piece of paper counts. Recycling bins located near the shed.

Woohoo Movember!

The best moustache at the end of November wins a prize!

The Fun World of Moustaches: Did you know that the world's largest moustache has been officially recorded by Guinness World Records as a whopping 4.29m (14ft) long?

Once upon a time, every house would have a Moustache Cup. These special cups provided a built-in ledge to protect the moustache from getting wet while sipping hot beverages — a practical solution for gentlemen wishing to keep their moustaches looking their best.

Moustache styles come in numerous variations, including the classic “handlebar,” “Fu Manchu,” “walrus,” and “pencil-thin” moustaches, each carrying its own unique charm. There are so many terms for moustache too — a Mo, a 'Tache or 'Stache, or slang like Cookie Duster or Whiskers. What will you grow yours to be?
